title: Practice Exam 10
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: At least how many seconds following distance should you keep behind the vehicle ahead under good conditions on the freeway?
choices: At least three seconds
At least one second
Exactly one-half second
No following distance is needed at freeway speeds
questions.explanation: Maintaining at least a three-second following distance gives you time to react and stop safely at freeway speeds, and more time is needed in poor conditions.

questions.question: A driver can be convicted of DUI even with a BAC below 0.08% if:
choices: Their driving is impaired by alcohol or drugs
They are over the age of 65
They were driving on a freeway
They have a clean driving record
questions.explanation: You can be arrested and convicted for DUI at any BAC if alcohol or drugs impair your ability to drive safely. The 0.08% level is a per se limit, not a safe threshold.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: Why is it important to keep your attention on driving rather than on a phone conversation?
choices: Distracted drivers are slower to notice hazards and react to them
Phone use improves reaction time
Conversations help you scan the road better
Talking on the phone has no measurable effect
questions.explanation: Distraction slows your ability to detect hazards and respond, increasing the chance of a collision.

questions.question: A steady yellow 'X' lane-control signal over your lane means what?
choices: The lane use is changing; move safely out of this lane
The lane is permanently a turn-only lane
You may speed up to clear the lane
The lane is reserved for buses
questions.explanation: A steady yellow 'X' warns that the lane assignment is about to change (for example, a reversible lane reversing direction), so prepare to move out of it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Control Signals

questions.question: You notice another vehicle traveling in your blind spot. What is the best action before changing lanes?
choices: Wait until that vehicle moves out of your blind spot and the lane is clear
Change lanes quickly before the vehicle catches up
Speed up so you are ahead and change lanes immediately
Honk and change lanes to force the other car back
questions.explanation: You should never change lanes while a vehicle is in your blind spot; wait until you can see it is clear of your path.

questions.question: A green downward-pointing arrow over a lane means what?
choices: You may drive in that lane
The lane is closed ahead
You must turn at the next intersection
The lane is reserved for emergency vehicles
questions.explanation: A green downward arrow in a lane-control signal indicates the lane is open and you may travel in it. A red 'X' would mean the lane is closed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Control Signals

questions.question: Talking with passengers can be a distraction primarily because it can cause:
choices: Cognitive distraction that takes your mind off driving
Mechanical failure of the vehicle
Manual distraction only
A reduction in fuel efficiency
questions.explanation: Conversations with passengers can divert your mental focus from the driving task, a form of cognitive distraction.

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign showing a truck on a downward slope warns of what?
choices: A steep downgrade ahead where trucks should use caution
A truck weigh station is open
Trucks are prohibited beyond this point
A truck loading zone is ahead
questions.explanation: The truck-on-a-hill warning sign indicates a steep downgrade; large vehicles should check brakes and reduce speed before descending.

questions.question: When you are carrying a heavy load or towing a trailer, how should you adjust your following distance?
choices: Increase it, because the extra weight lengthens your stopping distance
Decrease it, because the load helps you stop faster
Keep it the same as an unloaded vehicle
Only adjust it on downhill grades
questions.explanation: A heavy load or trailer increases your stopping distance, so you should allow more following distance.

questions.question: What is the correct order of actions when changing lanes?
choices: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, then change lanes
Change lanes, then signal once you are in the new lane
Look over your shoulder, change lanes, then signal
Speed up, change lanes, then check your mirrors
questions.explanation: The proper sequence is to signal your intention, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder for the blind spot, and then change lanes when it is clear.

questions.question: On a two-lane undivided highway, what is the maximum speed limit unless otherwise posted?
choices: 55 mph
65 mph
50 mph
60 mph
questions.explanation: Two-lane undivided highways have a maximum speed of 55 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: A blue painted curb is reserved for whom?
choices: Vehicles displaying a valid disabled person placard or license plate
Any vehicle for short passenger drop-off
Commercial loading and unloading only
Government and emergency vehicles only
questions.explanation: A blue curb is reserved for disabled persons and their drivers who display a valid placard or disabled-person license plate.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on most California freeways unless a higher limit is posted?
choices: 65 mph
70 mph
60 mph
75 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum freeway speed is 65 mph, although some freeways are posted at 70 mph. Never exceed the posted limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: If you must cross several lanes to change lanes, how should you do it?
choices: Change one lane at a time, signaling and checking for each move
Cross all the lanes at once in a single sweeping motion
Change lanes only at intersections
Cross without signaling to move faster
questions.explanation: When you need to cross several lanes, move one lane at a time, signaling and checking traffic and your blind spot before each change.

questions.question: On a slippery or icy road, how should you handle following distance?
choices: Allow much more following distance than the three-second minimum
Keep exactly three seconds, since the rule already accounts for it
Reduce following distance so you do not lose traction
Following distance does not matter on slippery roads
questions.explanation: On slippery roads it takes longer to stop, so you should increase your following distance well beyond three seconds.

questions.question: When pulling over for an approaching emergency vehicle, why is it important not to stop in an intersection?
choices: You should clear the intersection first so you do not block the emergency vehicle's path
Stopping in an intersection is faster
Intersections are the safest place to stop
Emergency vehicles never drive through intersections
questions.explanation: Never stop in an intersection; drive through it and pull to the right beyond it so you do not block traffic or the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: You are facing uphill on a street with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
choices: Toward the edge of the road
Away from the edge of the road
Straight ahead
Toward the center of the road
questions.explanation: With no curb, whether facing uphill or downhill, turn the wheels toward the edge or shoulder so the car rolls away from traffic.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on a Hill

questions.question: A streetcar, trolley, or train is approaching an intersection at the same time you are. Who has the right of way?
choices: The streetcar, trolley, or train always has the right of way
The vehicle on the right always has the right of way
Whichever arrives at the intersection first
The car, because rail vehicles must yield to automobiles
questions.explanation: You must always yield the right of way to streetcars, trolleys, trains, and other vehicles on rails because they cannot stop or maneuver quickly.

questions.question: If you find yourself becoming distracted or overwhelmed by activity inside the vehicle, the safest response is to:
choices: Find a safe place to pull over and stop until you can refocus
Speed up to finish the trip sooner
Close your eyes briefly to reset
Keep driving and try harder to concentrate
questions.explanation: When distractions inside the car become too much, the safest action is to pull over safely and address them before continuing.

questions.question: If you host a party and serve alcohol, you should:
choices: Make sure guests who have been drinking do not drive home
Encourage guests to drink quickly so they sober up sooner
Serve only at night so guests drive carefully
Let guests decide entirely on their own with no involvement
questions.explanation: As a social host you share responsibility for guests' safety. Arrange alternate rides or sober drivers so no impaired guest drives away.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: To use a carpool (HOV) lane during posted commuter hours, what must your vehicle generally have?
choices: The minimum number of occupants shown on the posted signs
At least one passenger under 18 years old
A commercial vehicle permit
Only the driver, since HOV lanes are for fast solo drivers
questions.explanation: Carpool/HOV lanes require the minimum number of people posted on the signs (for example two or more) during the hours indicated, unless your vehicle has a qualifying decal.

questions.question: When the yellow lights on a school zone sign are flashing, you should:
choices: Slow to the posted school zone speed and watch for children
Maintain your normal speed
Stop completely and wait
Treat it like a railroad crossing
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow lights on a school sign mean the reduced school-zone speed limit is in effect; slow to the posted limit and watch carefully for children.

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign showing a person walking warns of what?
choices: A pedestrian crossing area where you should watch for people on foot
A sidewalk closure ahead
A bus stop with passengers boarding
A jogging or fitness trail crosses the road
questions.explanation: The pedestrian-symbol warning sign means people may be crossing; slow down and be prepared to yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: On a road without sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?
choices: On the left side facing oncoming traffic
On the right side with traffic
In the center of the roadway
Wherever there is the most shade
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the left side of a road without sidewalks, facing oncoming traffic so they can see and react to approaching vehicles.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the signal light is green. What should you do?
choices: Obey the officer's directions, even if they contradict the green light
Follow the green light because signals override officers
Stop and wait until the officer leaves
Proceed only after honking to confirm with the officer
questions.explanation: You must always obey directions from a police officer or other person authorized to direct traffic, even over a traffic signal.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance when driving at night?
choices: Reduced visibility means you need more time and distance to see and react to hazards
Vehicles brake more quickly at night
Following distance rules only apply after dark
Your tires grip the road better at night
questions.explanation: At night you cannot see as far ahead, so a larger following distance gives you more time to react to hazards.

questions.question: A green-and-white sign with a route number inside a shield tells you what?
choices: Which highway or interstate route you are on or approaching
The speed limit for that highway
The distance to the next rest area
That the road is a designated scenic byway
questions.explanation: Route marker (shield) signs identify the numbered highway, interstate, or state route. They help with navigation but do not set speed limits.

questions.question: A school bus that has stopped with its red lights flashing means children are likely to:
choices: Be loading or unloading and may cross the road
Have already left the area
Be staying seated on the bus
Be waiting on the far sidewalk only
questions.explanation: Red flashing lights and an extended stop arm mean children are getting on or off the bus and may cross the road, so all required traffic must stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road / School Buses

questions.question: At a signal showing a green light (no arrow), when may you make a left turn?
choices: After yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when the way is clear
Immediately, because the green light gives left turns the right-of-way
Only if a green arrow also appears
Never; a green light prohibits left turns
questions.explanation: On a solid green, a left turn is permissive: you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and turn only when it is safe. A green arrow would give you a protected turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: When approaching a school zone where children are present, what speed should you not exceed within 500 to 1,000 feet of the school where so posted?
choices: The posted reduced limit, which can be as low as 25 mph or less when children are present
Always 40 mph regardless of posting
Whatever speed the surrounding street allows
55 mph if it is a through street
questions.explanation: School zones use posted reduced limits (commonly 25 mph, sometimes 15 mph) when children are present; obey the sign and slow down accordingly.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: You are parked facing downhill on a street with a curb. Which way should the front wheels point?
choices: Toward the curb
Away from the curb
Straight ahead
Slightly away from the curb
questions.explanation: Facing downhill with a curb, turn the wheels toward the curb so the vehicle rolls into the curb if it moves.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on a Hill

questions.question: Bicyclists traveling on a roadway are required to:
choices: Obey the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers
Follow pedestrian rules instead of traffic laws
Ride only against the flow of traffic
Yield to all vehicles at all times
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and must obey the same traffic laws and signals.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway from an on-ramp?
choices: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic, then merge into a gap
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large opening
Enter slowly and let freeway traffic adjust to you
Merge into the far-left lane as soon as you reach the freeway
questions.explanation: On the on-ramp and acceleration lane, build your speed to match freeway traffic, then signal and merge into a gap without stopping.

questions.question: A pedestrian steps into an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection ahead of you. You must:
choices: Yield the right of way to the pedestrian
Continue because only marked crosswalks count
Speed up to clear the intersection first
Sound your horn and proceed
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist at intersections whether or not they are painted, and you must yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren on and red lights flashing. What should you do?
choices: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
Speed up to clear the intersection ahead of it
Stop immediately wherever you are, even in the middle of an intersection
Continue at your normal speed and ignore it
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping until they have passed. Never stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When dropping off children at school, the safest practice is to:
choices: Let them out at the curb in the designated drop-off zone
Stop in the traffic lane to save time
Let them exit on the traffic side of the car
Drop them across the street to avoid the line
questions.explanation: Always drop children off at the curb in the designated loading zone so they do not step into traffic.
